maddhapara: The footprint's own NDVI fell in the early 1990s and has been roughly flat since, while the surrounding farmland greened significantly. The strong relative decline, more extreme than every placebo, therefore means that the mine compound did not follow its surroundings rather than that it kept losing vegetation. This fits an underground mine whose surface footprint (offices, plant, stockpiles; 89% built-up in Dynamic World) was established and then stayed developed. The 2011 change point is driven mainly by the ring greening after 2011, not by a step at the site, so it should not be read as the date of a mining event.
hambach: This is the clearest case. Footprint NDVI fell steadily from about 0.52 in 1990 to about 0.23, while the ring showed no significant trend, and 61% of the footprint's vegetated pixels were lost compared with 8% of the ring's. The relative slope was about three times steeper than the steepest placebo. A gradual decline with a 2006 change point is consistent with an open pit advancing across the footprint over decades rather than one clearing event. Because the footprint is the present-day outline, it includes land that was still forest or farmland in 1990.
bingham-canyon: The footprint was already largely bare in 1990 (NDVI about 0.15), as expected for a mine operating since the early 20th century, and declined further to about 0.08 while the ring greened slightly. The relative trend was more extreme than all 14 usable placebos; 6 placebo copies were skipped: one fell on open water (the Great Salt Lake) and five on more than 30% bare ground, which is common in this semi-arid landscape. The small absolute changes show that NDVI is close to its floor here: further expansion onto bare dumps is hard to see in a vegetation index.
threshold: Agreement was weakest at Maddhapara, where NDVI > 0.3 labelled almost all built-up village land with trees and gardens as vegetated (non-vegetated producer's agreement below 0.10), and best at Bingham Canyon, where the contrast between bare rock and scrub is sharp. A single global threshold is therefore unreliable for mapping vegetation loss in densely settled, tree-rich landscapes, and the vegetation-loss figures above should be read as indicative, with the footprint-versus-ring comparison mattering more than the absolute hectares.
general: In all three cases the mine footprint's relative trend lay outside the placebo distribution, while most placebos would have passed a conventional significance test. The practical lesson for monitoring studies is that a site-minus-control trend with p < 0.05 is a weak criterion; it should be compared with what the same method produces at locations without a mine. With about 20 placebos the evidence is limited to p ≈ 0.05 per site, so the conclusions are that the footprint trends are unusual relative to their surroundings, not that their size has been estimated precisely or that every change inside a footprint was caused by mining.
